decisions.justification: Q1 explicitly asked what to do when a target exists, and the user chose aborting before changes while reporting every clash.
Q2 and Q5 asked whether failures permit partial completion and how broadly transactional protection must apply; the user required staging, rollback, and no half-renamed directory.
Q4 addressed exact source-to-same-target no-ops, but nobody decided whether files already matching the overall target naming scheme belong in the rename set.
Q3 explicitly asked about a destination occupied by another source in the same plan, and the user chose collision-and-abort.
The transcript never asked or settled what a second identical successful invocation should do.
No question or repository-based resolution addressed case-only renames on case-insensitive filesystems.
Q8 asked when and where success and failure output should appear, and multiple later questions settled recovery diagnostics and nonzero exits.
The session never asked or settled whether preview or confirmation should be part of the fix.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: a run that cannot complete leaves every file unchanged
no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session exhaustively negotiated transactional execution, crash recovery, locking, and diagnostics, and the implementation visibly reflects those choices. It over-expanded an expected bounded fix into an architectural journal-and-recovery system, used a final approval gate, and missed self-inclusion, repeat-run idempotency, case-only filesystem behavior, and preview policy.
